purpose: one row per catalogue source entry, recording the legacy statute or provision, the existing source IDs and legacy rule references, the established jurisdiction associations, the broadly relevant reporting issue or rule purpose, the existing operational mapping and the remaining implementation dependencies
authority_basis: owner directive recorded by PHASE5-001O: the relevant statutes in the legacy system are OWNER_ACCEPTED_LEGAL_AUTHORITY; missing provenance, historical versions and prior-review records are not prerequisites for accepting them; broadly relevant statutory provisions are included, and a provision may support more than one rule, jurisdiction or report condition where the legacy corpus establishes that relationship
acceptance_statement: Acceptance recorded here is owner-directed. This order performed no independent legal verification, no re-review of the statutes and no provenance investigation. The digest check reported in admitted_artifacts.json is a custody fact about which bytes are on disk, not a legal conclusion.

duplicate_bookkeeping_and_count_status.statement: An exact corpus-wide unique-legal-provision count is not asserted here. Under the recorded owner directive the count is bookkeeping: it is carried as an administrative limitation and does not block acceptance of the statutes or coverage planning.

field_notes.legacy_rule_references: A reference is recorded only where an exact recorded string basis exists between the catalogue entry and a legacy record, and each row names the basis it used. A row with no basis records NOT_ESTABLISHED and carries LEGACY_OPERATIONAL_MAPPING_NOT_ESTABLISHED as an implementation dependency. Nothing was inferred, normalised or broadened.
field_notes.broadly_relevant_reporting_issue_or_purp: Composed from the ratified source-family label, the catalogue record type, the recorded instrument title and, where available, the recorded legacy subject. No legal meaning was invented.
field_notes.remaining_implementation_dependencies: Work items; each is a task to perform against the accepted corpus, not a reason to reject it.
field_notes.administrative_limitations: Recorded limitations of the legacy recordkeeping. Under the owner directive they are limitations only and are not acceptance prerequisites.

legacy_rule_references.section: Art. 1203 (31 L.P.R.A. § 9495) — personal actions of EVERY type prescribe in FOUR years unless another period is specifically provided, so one article answers all three classes. ⚠️ TWO THINGS RECORDED, NEITHER DISPLACING THIS PERIOD: **Art. 1814's TRANSITION rule** preserves the FORMER limitations duration for a period already RUNNING when the 2020 Code took effect on 28 November 2020 — unless that period was subsequently interrupted, in which case the new Code's duration applies; and **Act 98-2026** restricts medical-debt credit REPORTING and certain collection practices, which the owner records as establishing no different limitations period
legacy_rule_references.starts: four years measured from the printed headline last-payment date by the OWNER accrual rule (AMENDMENT-011), and withheld entirely when it is not printed. ⚖️ ART. 1814 IS NOW AUTHORISED BUT NOT YET VALUED — owner ruling, 2026-09-17: "use the old period". A period already RUNNING on 28 November 2020 keeps the FORMER limitations duration, and an interruption switches the clock to the new Code's duration; so a pre-2020, uninterrupted debt is governed by the FORMER duration and this row's FOUR years is only the current one. ⚠️ WHY THE RULING IS NOT APPLIED AS A NUMBER: the former duration's VALUE has not been supplied or read anywhere in this repository, and inventing one is what the truth contract forbids — so the pre-2020 branch is recorded as authorised-with-value-outstanding rather than assumed. ⚠️ The direction of the open defect is OVER-assertion for a pre-2020 item whose true duration is longer than four years; nothing else about this row moves.

legacy_rule_references.section: Va. Code § 8.01-246(A)(2) — an action upon a contract IN WRITING AND SIGNED by the party to be charged, FIVE years. ⚖️ The three-year branch, § 8.01-246(A)(4), remains the provision for a contract that is not in writing, or is in writing but NOT SIGNED by the party to be charged — recorded here rather than applied
legacy_rule_references.starts: five years measured from the printed headline last-payment date by the OWNER accrual rule (AMENDMENT-011), and withheld entirely when it is not printed. ⚖️ WHY THIS BRANCH — owner ruling, 2026-09-17: the owner's logic is that an UNSIGNED contract for debt would never appear on a credit bureau, so a debt that IS reported is one the SIGNED-contract timing governs. That is why (A)(2)'s five years is asserted here, with (A)(4)'s three years recorded as the branch for a contract shown to be unwritten or unsigned

legacy_rule_references.section: Va. Code § 8.01-246(B) — MEDICAL DEBT, three years, measured from the DUE DATE OF THE FINAL INVOICE; ⚖️ the statute expressly DEFINES the covered medical debt, and it carries a separate PAYMENT-PLAN rule: where a provider payment plan allows a longer collection period, a breach of that plan produces a THREE-year period running from the debtor's breach
legacy_rule_references.starts: three years measured from the printed headline last-payment date by the OWNER accrual rule (AMENDMENT-011), and withheld entirely when it is not printed. ⚠️ The statute's own start is the DUE DATE OF THE FINAL INVOICE, which a report does not print; a printed last payment is normally LATER than that due date, so the measured age is YOUNGER than the statutory one — under-assertion, never over-assertion. ⚖️ The payment-plan breach limb is recorded and NOT applied: whether a provider payment plan existed, and when the debtor breached it, are not printed facts.
